To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed profiled support vector machine approach produces more accurate models than do the standard support vector machine and multilayer perceptrons for predicting the blood concentration of cyclosporine A, which is an immunosuppressive drug commonly used in the treatment of renal transplant recipients.

we have developed a profile-dependent support vector machine approach that improves the results from a standard SVM, and we have demonstrated its usefulness in the prediction and detection of Cyclosporine blood concentrations in kidney transplant recipients.
we have developed an accurate, robust, and understandable model for predicting CyA blood concentrations in kidney recipients using PD-SVM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of SVMs for TDM of kidney recipients, with a twofold goal: prediction and detection.
the development of a methodology for therapeutic drug monitoring of kidney transplant recipients using profiled support vector machines.
the development and validation of a new methodology based on the SVM approach to TDM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PD-SVM is a very useful and promising approach for TDM in renal transplantation.
the PD-SV approach is more accurate and robust than other models, specially when a large number of classes are involved, such as in the one-again-all scheme.
SVMs outperform MLPs in terms of accuracy and robustness in both the prediction and detection of CyA blood concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a software tool that allows the physician to monitor the drug concentration in a kidney transplant recipient, in order to adjust the dose of the drug to the patient.
SVMs are very promising in TDM and can be considered as an alternative to neural networks.
the PD-SV model is the one that better predicts CyA concentration and is robust in the presence additive noise, and that it can be used for therapeutic drug monitoring in the clinical environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SVM approach is a promising tool for TDM of kidney transplant recipients, especially when a priori knowledge is incorporated into the model.
PD-SVMs are able to produce more accurate and robust prediction models for CyA blood concentration than do neural networks, specially in the one- against-all scheme.
the SVM approach is more accurate than the neural network approach in the prediction of CyA blood concentration, especially in the one-again-all scheme.
